# Triangle Inequality — Never Gain Distance by Detouring

## The identity to remember

$$
|a+b|\le|a|+|b|
$$

**Every symbol explained:** a,b are real numbers; absolute bars denote magnitude; |a+b| is magnitude after combining signed movements.

**Substitute actual numbers:** For a=−7,b=3, |a+b|=4; |a|+|b|=7+3=10. A forward and backward move reduces net distance.

## Why it is true

The upper bounds −|a|≤a≤|a| and −|b|≤b≤|b| combine to −(|a|+|b|)≤a+b≤|a|+|b|. Thus the net magnitude cannot exceed the sum of magnitudes.

## Algorithm or number puzzle application

Use in Manhattan distance, absolute differences and proofs of lower bounds for travel or movement problems.

## Assumptions and pitfalls

A path of 3 right, 7 left has length 10 but displacement magnitude 4; minimum route between endpoints may be shorter than the travelled path.

## Your turn

In vector spaces the relevant norm also obeys triangle inequality; do not substitute unrelated operations that are not norms.

**Memory rule:** Translate the inequality into a statement about maximum, minimum or impossible values, then prove it.
